paper_title: Exclusion of ALP Cogenesis Dark Matter in a Mass Window Above 100 $μ$eV
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis (canonical axion-photon coupling)
notes: ORGAN Phase 1b haloscope experiment searching for axion dark matter in the 107.42–111.93 μeV mass range (25.97–27.07 GHz). The paper reports an exclusion limit of g_agamma ≥ 4×10^-12 GeV^-1 at 95% CL, representing the best upper bound to date in this mass region and sufficient to exclude the ALP cogenesis dark matter model. The limit is mass-independent across the scanned range, so encoded as a horizontal line at the two mass boundaries. Local dark matter density assumed to be ρ_a ≈ 0.45 GeV/cm³ (100% axion). Uncertainty on coupling: δg_agamma ≈ 6.1%. The experiment used a tunable rectangular cavity with TM110 mode, achieving QL ~ 3700 and form factor C ~ 0.40. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.92, 35)) | Vision: The exclusion plot (FIG. 5) shows the upper exclusion limits on g_agamma from ORGAN Phase 1b at 95% CL in the mass range 107.42–111.93 μeV (25.97–27.07 GHz). The x-axis is frequency in GHz (linear scale, 25.5–27.5 GHz range); converted to mass using m[eV] = 4.136e-15 * f[Hz]. The y-axis is g_agamma in GeV^-1 (log scale, 1e-12 to 1e-10). The blue shaded region represents the ORGAN Phase 1b exclusion zone. The yellow band shows the ALP cogenesis model prediction. The CAST limit (gray) is also shown for reference. The boundary traced is the lower edge of the blue exclusion region, which represents the minimum coupling excluded at each mass. The notch at ~26 GHz is noted in the text as due to insufficient integration time early in the data-taking run.
